description: Debug 32-bit (x86) .NET and .NET Framework apps, WinForms included, with Visual Studio-style tools: exception settings, Parallel Stacks, heap snapshots, WinForms control tools and more. Bundles an x86 build of netcoredbg.
config.sourceLink.enabled: When the program stops in a file that is not on this machine and the PDB has a Source Link map (as most NuGet packages built from GitHub have), download the file (cached in the extension's storage) and open it.
config.symbolServers: Symbol servers that "Download Symbols" (Modules view) asks for the PDB of an assembly without symbols.
config.title: .NET x86 Debugger
config.debuggerPath: Full path to an x86 netcoredbg.exe. When empty, the bundled x86 build is used.
config.trace: Troubleshooting: log the debug adapter protocol traffic to the ".NET x86 Debugger" output channel and write a netcoredbg log file (its path is shown in that channel).
config.memoryGraph.autoOpen: Open the memory / CPU graph automatically when a dotnet-x86 debug session starts.
config.dump.maxDepth: Maximum nesting depth expanded by Dump Variable / Dump Expression.
config.dump.maxNodes: Dump Variable / Dump Expression stops expanding further objects once this many values have been collected. Large objects (e.g. a Form) have hundreds of members per level.
debugger.label: .NET x86 (netcoredbg)
debugger.launch.program: Path to the x86 .exe (or a framework-dependent .dll, launched with the x86 dotnet host).
debugger.attach.processId: Process ID to attach to. Use ${command:pickProcess} to pick from a list.
snippet.launch.label: .NET x86: Launch
snippet.attach.label: .NET x86: Attach
config.stepHistory.enabled: Record the location and local variables at every stop in the Step History view. Off: the view is hidden.
debugger.attach.processName: Name of the x86 .NET process to attach to (with or without ".exe"). Debugging waits until it starts. Used when processId is not set.
debugger.attach.waitTimeout: Seconds to wait for processName to start.
snippet.waitAttach.label: .NET x86: Attach when the process starts
snippet.waitAttach.description: Wait for a 32-bit .NET process by name and attach to it
config.uiFreeze.enabled: Pause the program when its UI stops responding (a UI thread does not process window messages for dotnetX86.uiFreeze.thresholdMs), showing the code that holds it up.
config.uiFreeze.thresholdMs: How long (ms) a UI thread may not respond before the program is paused.
config.heapSnapshot.collectGarbage: Run a garbage collection right before taking a heap snapshot, so that it holds only objects that are still reachable.
config.perfTips.enabled: Show the elapsed time at the end of the stopped line after a step or continue (PerfTips).
command.breakOnExceptionType: Break When This Type Is Thrown
config.exceptionLog.captureLocals: With the exception log on, also record the call stack and the locals of the first frames of your code with each exception (up to 200 per session). Turn off if an app that throws very many exceptions runs too slowly.
config.exceptionLog.enabled: Record every exception thrown in the debuggee (including caught ones) in the Exception Log view and the Debug Console, without stopping. Applies to new debug sessions. Apps that throw very many exceptions run slower while it is on. Off: the view is hidden.
debugger.launch.sourceFileMap: Maps the source paths recorded in PDBs to folders on this machine: `{ "PDB path prefix": "local folder" }`, e.g. `{ "C:\\build\\MyLib": "D:\\work\\MyLib", "/_/": "D:\\work\\MyLib\\" }`. The longest matching prefix wins; case and `/` `\\` do not matter.
debugger.launch.sourceSearchPaths: Folders searched (with their subfolders) for source files whose PDB path does not exist on this machine. The file whose trailing folders match the PDB path best is used; when several match equally, none is.
debugger.attach.sourceFileMap: Maps the source paths recorded in PDBs to folders on this machine: `{ "PDB path prefix": "local folder" }`, e.g. `{ "C:\\build\\MyLib": "D:\\work\\MyLib", "/_/": "D:\\work\\MyLib\\" }`. The longest matching prefix wins; case and `/` `\\` do not matter.
debugger.attach.sourceSearchPaths: Folders searched (with their subfolders) for source files whose PDB path does not exist on this machine. The file whose trailing folders match the PDB path best is used; when several match equally, none is.
config.sourceFileMap: Same as `sourceFileMap` in launch.json, for every configuration (launch.json entries win for the same prefix). `${workspaceFolder}` and `${userHome}` can be used.
config.sourceSearchPaths: Same as `sourceSearchPaths` in launch.json, for every configuration (both lists are searched). `${workspaceFolder}` and `${userHome}` can be used.
walkthrough.title: Get started with the .NET x86 Debugger
walkthrough.description: Set up this machine and your project, and debug a 32-bit .NET app.
walkthrough.environment.title: Check the environment
walkthrough.environment.description:
See whether the x86 .NET runtimes and the .NET SDK are installed, and what is missing.
[Check Environment](command:dotnetX86.checkEnvironment)
walkthrough.project.title: Make the project x86
walkthrough.project.description:
The exe must be built as x86 and write a Portable PDB. The environment check fixes the project file for you.
[Check the Projects](command:dotnetX86.checkEnvironment)
walkthrough.launch.title: Create launch.json
walkthrough.launch.description:
Debug configurations and a build task, made from your .csproj files.
[Generate launch.json](command:dotnetX86.generateLaunchJson)
walkthrough.debug.title: Start debugging
walkthrough.debug.description:
Set a breakpoint and press F5.
[Start Debugging](command:workbench.action.debug.start)
walkthrough.features.title: Explore the features
walkthrough.features.description:
Exceptions, threads, memory, WinForms controls and more, with use cases.
[Open the Guide](https://takahino.github.io/vscode-dotnet-x86-debugger/usage.html)
config.memoryGraph.enabled: Sample the memory, CPU, GDI / USER objects, handles and 32-bit address space of the program while debugging (Memory / CPU graph).
config.inlineValues.enabled: Show the values of variables at the end of the lines while stopped (inline values).
config.autos.enabled: Show the Autos view (variables of the current and previous line).
config.modules.enabled: Show the Modules view, with Download Symbols and Decompile for Debugging.
config.exceptionSettings.enabled: Show the Exception Settings view, and stop on the exception types checked in it.
config.winforms.enabled: Show the WinForms Controls view: Highlight on Screen, Break on Event, Change Property and Show Data Bindings.
config.heapSnapshot.enabled: Heap Snapshots, with the GDI leak candidates (Call Stack context menu and Command Palette).
config.parallelStacks.enabled: Parallel Stacks, and Freeze / Thaw Thread in the Call Stack context menu.
config.valueTrend.enabled: Value trend and section timing (Track Value, Start / End Timer Here in the editor context menu).
config.pinnedValues.enabled: Pinned values: expressions pinned to an editor line, evaluated at every stop.
config.breakpointCommands.enabled: Temporary, dependent, when-changed and caller-filtered breakpoints in the editor context menu (the #once, #after, #changed and #caller conditions keep working).
config.variableTools.enabled: Commands in the Variables / Watch context menu: Dump, View as Table / Image, Copy as C#, View String, snapshots and Make Object ID.
config.generateTest.enabled: Generate Unit Test from Here in the Call Stack context menu.
config.sessionReport.enabled: Export Debug Session Report (Step History view title and Command Palette).
